issues.title: Time-continuity norm estimate

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, we can redefine $\psi(t^*) := \psi^*$, without breaking the property \eqref{eq:time_continuity_nabla}.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma claims both qualitative continuity and a bound of the C(H1) norm by the L2(H2) norm and the L2(H^{-2}) norm of partial_t Delta psi. The old proof establishes the continuous representative and then stops; it never controls its supremum norm. Thus the argument supports only the qualitative part of the statement, not the quantitative estimate subsequently used in the existence-and-stability theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous embedding's quantitative bound, and consequently the C(H1) component of the stated existence-and-stability estimate, lacks a proof. The qualitative continuity result remains established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Complete Lemma lemm:H1_continuity with the standard local norm estimate obtained from its existing mollified energy identity. Apply the identity to ψ itself, bound the time integral by the L²(H⁻²) norm of ∂tΔψ times the L²(H²₀) norm of ψ, average over the comparison time, and use H²₀→H¹₀ and Young's inequality. This gives the stated C(H¹₀) bound, which can then be combined with the theorem's existing L²(H²₀) and time-derivative estimates to recover its full stability estimate unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The quantitative estimate is genuinely unproved, so this is not a typo. However, it follows by a short, routine extension of an identity already used in the lemma; no new lemma, proof architecture, hypothesis, or weakening is needed, and the dependent existence-and-stability theorem retains exactly the same guarantee.

issues.title: Stokes-to-stream source sign
issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims that the scalar stream-function datum is f=curl(g). The introduction, after applying negative scalar curl to the Stokes equation, establishes f=-curl(g). The difference reverses the forcing associated with a given Stokes problem, although the displayed norm estimates in the remark are insensitive to this sign.
issues.overall_effect: The prose maps a Stokes force to the wrong signed stream-function force. The sign-insensitive stability bounds themselves remain unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the remark's datum f = curl(g) by f = −curl(g). Leave its stability bounds unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The introduction explicitly derives f = −curl(g) by applying negative scalar curl to the Stokes equation, so the correction is uniquely forced by the old source. The later occurrence is a transcriptional sign error, and none of the norm estimates depends on that sign.

issues.title: Auxiliary best-approximation bound
issues.failure_explanation: The announced intermediate estimate invokes v, which is neither defined nor quantified in the theorem or proof. Galerkin orthogonality and the subsequent J1 calculation instead yield a term involving psi-chi_kh. Read literally, the displayed estimate is undefined and cannot serve as the stated bridge to the final triangle inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem's proof contains a malformed key intermediate bound, and the later convergence-rate theorem invokes that main result. The surrounding calculations nevertheless force a unique correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In equation eq:error_fully_discrete_chikh, replace the undefined term ∇(v−χ_kh) by ∇(ψ−χ_kh). No other proof change is needed; the J1 estimate already produces this term, after which the stated triangle inequality and the dependent convergence-rate theorem remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The symbol v is nowhere defined or quantified, while the immediately preceding Galerkin-orthogonality calculation uniquely yields ψ−χ_kh. This is a malformed copied symbol whose correction is forced directly by the old proof and requires no repair of its mathematical reasoning.

issues.title: C0 interior-penalty regularity domain

failure_location.quote: The space $X$ in this case is given by $H^2_0(\Om)\cap H^{\frac52-\varepsilon}(\Om)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that X, and consequently the domain of the Ritz projection, is H^2_0 intersected with H^{5/2-epsilon}. The old remark instead identifies the same X for theta=1/2-epsilon as H^2_0 intersected with H^{5/2+epsilon}. Moreover, the displayed edge construction requires traces of second derivatives, which are not generally available below the 5/2 threshold. Thus the later prose improperly enlarges the claimed domain across that threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The C0 subsection overstates the class on which its edge form and Ritz projection are well-defined. The later H^3-based convergence result does not need the overstated lower-regularity domain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both occurrences of H²₀(Ω)∩H^(5/2−ε)(Ω) in the C⁰ interior-penalty subsection, including the stated Ritz-projection domain, by H²₀(Ω)∩H^(5/2+ε)(Ω). The later H³-based convergence result requires no change.
issues.why_classification: The old paper's earlier assumptions remark already identifies the same space X with exponent 5/2+ε, and the displayed classical edge averages require regularity above the 5/2 trace threshold. Thus the later minus sign is a uniquely forced exponent transcription; the purported lower-regularity cases could not make the displayed form well-defined, so correcting it does not surrender a coherent guarantee.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: As mentioned above, the space $X$ in this case is given by $H^2_0(\Om)\cap H^{\frac52+\varepsilon}(\Om)$.

issues.title: Boundary average in the interior-penalty form

failure_location.quote: \jump{\frac{\pa v}{\pa n}} =-\frac{\pa v}{\pa n_e}\quad \text{and}\quad\avg{\frac{\pa^2 v}{\pa n^2}} = -\frac{\pa^2 v}{\pa n_e^2}.

issues.failure_explanation: For a smooth clamped solution, elementwise integration by parts of the Hessian term produces the boundary contribution +∫∂Ω (partial_nn psi)(partial_n w). The old convention gives both the average and jump a minus sign, so their product in the added consistency term is again positive and reinforces rather than cancels that contribution. Consequently the defined C0 form does not satisfy the asserted discrete consistency assumption, which is the premise used to prove the C0 specialization of the convergence theorem. A positive boundary average combined with the retained negative jump gives the required cancellation.
issues.overall_effect: The C0 interior-penalty specialization, including its cited Ritz estimate and O(k+h^2) convergence conclusion, is not justified for the form as printed. The abstract conditional theory and the C1 specialization are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For a boundary edge, retain jump(∂v/∂n) = −∂v/∂n_e but define avg(∂²v/∂n²) = +∂²v/∂n_e². Use this corrected convention in the interior-penalty form and Ritz projection. A direct elementwise integration-by-parts check then shows cancellation of the boundary consistency term, restoring ass:discrete_bilin_form and the stated O(k+h²) C⁰ convergence specialization.
issues.why_classification: The printed signs define an actually inconsistent bilinear form, so repairing the consistency inference requires mathematical checking and is more than a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, one local sign correction and a routine integration-by-parts verification restore the complete C⁰ chain with the same hypotheses, method, and convergence rate; no new architecture or mathematical loss is involved.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: \jump{\frac{\pa v}{\pa n}} =-\frac{\pa v}{\pa n_e}\quad \text{and}\quad\avg{\frac{\pa^2 v}{\pa n^2}} = \frac{\pa^2 v}{\pa n_e^2}.

issues.title: Pressure potential in the numerical example

failure_location.quote: only the pressure changes to $\tilde p = p + 10^5 (1.49 \cdot x_1^{1.49})^{-1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that adding 10^5 x_1^{-0.49} in the first force component changes the pressure by 10^5(1.49 x_1^{1.49})^{-1}. The Stokes equation requires the gradient of the pressure increment to equal the added force. Differentiating the old expression gives -10^5 x_1^{-2.49}, while differentiating 10^5·0.51^{-1}x_1^{0.51} gives the prescribed 10^5 x_1^{-0.49}. Thus the exact pressure asserted for the benchmark is wrong.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical example states the wrong exact pressure and therefore misidentifies the pressure used in its approximation-error explanation. The same-velocity and pressure-robustness conclusions remain valid because the prescribed force perturbation is still a gradient.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the asserted pressure increment by 10⁵·0.51⁻¹·x₁^0.51, up to the usual additive pressure constant, and update the accompanying pressure-error explanation accordingly. Retain the same velocity solution and pressure-robustness conclusion.
issues.why_classification: Obtaining the pressure requires the elementary but genuine calculation of an antiderivative of x₁^−0.49; the printed expression differentiates to the wrong force and therefore is not merely a copied symbol. The correction is short and local, while the force perturbation remains a gradient and all velocity and pressure-robustness conclusions remain unchanged.
